description: Search orderable platform products (default 10 rows, limit up to 20; a 'more' note means the page was full; one call is enough: every orderable row states price, requires_destination, needs_inquiry and open_denom as true/false). needs_inquiry=true means a bill or destination check is required first (BPJS, PDAM, PLN postpaid, e-wallet top-up; such rows often have price_type=open because the amount comes from the inquiry): prepare_purchase runs it for you. open_denom=true means the BUYER states the amount (amount parameter, min Rp1,000, for example an e-wallet top-up); the two are independent. A row with available=false and sold_out=true is a real product whose stock is empty right now: say so, never order it, it carries no ref. catalogue is a group key from the platform capability list (catalogue_groups, returned by discover_babelii), e.g. phone-credit, data-voucher, data-package, token, game, bills; omit it when unsure. A range such as 1-3 days means min_validity_days=1 and max_validity_days=3. Sort: relevance, price_asc, value_per_gb_day. For a voucher without a target number use data-voucher and requires_destination=false. Missing coverage/operator must not be guessed. Amounts may be written as 2000, 2.000, 2rb, 2 ribu or 2k. For an e-wallet top-up (Dana, GoPay, OVO, ShopeePay, LinkAja) with an amount, a fixed denomination that matches comes first; when there is none, the wallet's open_denom product comes first and its row carries amount_hint: use that product with amount=<the nominal> in prepare_purchase, do not guess a nearby denomination (the price is known only at prepare_purchase). open_denom=true lists only buyer-typed-nominal products, false only fixed ones.
name: search_products
title: Cari produk
